summary: Clearwater NF camp with two patrol trees from the 1920s, now ruins; the record's coordinates sit about 60 miles north of Lowell.

facts.status_note: Listed as ruins; no source gives a date or cause of loss

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as drive-up ruins; no source describes access today

events.note: Camp with two patrol trees (firelookout.com, Forest Service) or two patrol points (Idaho Fire Lookouts), dated to the 1920s

evidence.supports: 1920s camp with two patrol trees one mile ESE; now ruins
evidence.quote: 1920s: camp with 2 patrol trees 1 mile ESE. Ruins.

evidence.supports: Two patrol points one mile east-south-east
Table row gives the camp's build date as 1920
evidence.quote: Sec22 T34N camp 1920a Camp with two patrol trees

corrections.proposed: verify; about 9 miles north of Lowell, which is roughly 46.27, -115.6 by arithmetic from Lowell's listed coordinates
corrections.why: firelookout.com places the site 9 miles north of Lowell; the recorded point is about 60 miles north of Lowell
All three sources describe a camp with patrol trees or points, not a tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and the Forest Service say two patrol trees; Idaho Fire Lookouts says two patrol points one mile east-south-east. The story reports each source's wording.

notes_for_editor: The recorded point (47.00907, -115.73377) does not fit the firelookout.com description of 9 miles north of Lowell. Lowell is listed at 46.14389, -115.59694 on Wikipedia (not cited in the story), so the recorded point is about 60 miles north of it. This looks like a bad geocode and should be fixed before the map pin is used. The sources give no date or cause for the ruins, and no staffing. The Forest Service list gives Sec22 T34N R7E, which the story reports as section 22, township 34 north, range 7 east. That township is not checked against a map here, so it is a second clue, not a location.
